title: GGPEN satellite mission control centre (MCC)
locator: Capacidade para operar até três satélites em simultâneo, including the list of MCC functions

quantities.quantity: Maximum number of satellites the centre can operate simultaneously

conditions: The Angolan ground control centre monitors the ANGOSAT-2 telecommunications satellite. Its continuous monitoring is a ground-service capability.
supports: A precedent for recording subsystem telemetry and diagnosing faults from a control room.
limits: The source contains no public rover hardware specifications, rover fault-response times or Earth–Moon communications link budget.

title: CONAE deep-space stations and receiver specifications
locator: Section 6, Detalle del Equipamiento Disponible, Estación CLTC-CONAE-NEUQUEN, (a) Antena y receptores
conditions: Ground receive equipment at the Argentina–China Neuquén station. The page also lists a different station at Malargüe.
supports: A real ground endpoint for lunar communications planning. The listed receive bands can be checked against a proposed transmitting system.
limits: A ground antenna specification supplies neither a rover transmit power nor an available relay, data rate or coverage guarantee.

title: Argentina reports tracking support for Chinese lunar and Mars missions
locator: Paragraph beginning «La Estación CLTC-CONAE-NEUQUÉN brindó soporte»
conditions: Argentina's account of ground support to Chang’e and Tianwen-1 through the joint Neuquén station.
supports: Distinguishes an actual deep-space ground-support contribution from ownership of the lunar and Mars rover vehicles.
limits: This account does not specify a direct radio link between a rover and Neuquén, contact durations, or rover radio characteristics.

title: Bahrain’s report to COPUOS on navigation cameras for Rashid Rover 3
locator: A/AC.105/1337, Bahrain submission dated 27 October 2024, p. 6, Space segment, paragraph 1(c)
role: lunar rover navigation payload under development

quantities.quantity: Navigation cameras in Bahrain's Rashid Rover 3 contribution

conditions: Bahrain's national submission describes collaboration with the UAE's Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre on the Rashid Rover 3 lunar mission.
supports: A direct example of navigation and science cameras supplied by a partner to a lunar rover.
limits: Bahrain supplied the camera development effort. The report gives no camera field of view, stereo baseline, hazard detection accuracy, or surface performance.

title: Bahrain’s 2025 update on lunar surface and orbital instruments
locator: A/AC.105/1367, Bahrain submission dated 21 October 2025, p. 3, final two paragraphs of Space segment
role: lunar rover navigation payload development update
conditions: Bahrain reported developing the four surface-rover cameras. A separate joint hyperspectral instrument with Egypt is intended for a lunar orbiter.
supports: Distinguishes the navigation camera contribution from orbital mineral and ice mapping.
limits: The submission describes planned mounting and launch. It supplies no in-situ imagery or camera acceptance-test data.

title: AEB 2023 management report on Brazil’s integration and test facility
locator: Printed p. 61, Laboratório de Integração e Testes (LIT), text above Figure 31

quantities.quantity: Reported upper satellite mass for the facility's integration and environmental tests

conditions: AEB describes INPE's Brazilian satellite integration facility and lists thermal-vacuum, electromagnetic, vibration, acoustic, shock and mass-property work.
supports: A documented precedent for checking structure, mass properties, electronics and thermal response with complementary tests.
limits: This is a laboratory satellite mass limit. The source contains no qualifying test result or mass requirement for a planetary rover.

title: Brazilian space programme test facility, INPE LIT thermal-vacuum laboratory
locator: Principais Meios de Testes, item (a), Câmara de Simulação Espacial 6m x 8m
conditions: The facility operator INPE specifies a high-vacuum chamber with a zoned thermal shroud. AEB identifies this facility in its programme report (aeb-01).
supports: Defines an example equipment envelope for a future subsystem thermal-vacuum test.
limits: Chamber capability alone establishes no rover survival temperature, test cycle, or qualification result.

title: NASRDA Centre for Space Transport and Propulsion reports structural integration and test work
locator: Technical Divisions at CSTP & Activities, sections 2 (Structural Integration Systems) and 4 (Project Division)
conditions: Ground and flight preparation for a Nigerian rocket test in April 2019 included integration at CSTP and final checks on the launch platform.
supports: An example of separating fabrication, integrated checks, and safety and quality-control responsibilities in a test plan.
limits: This was a rocket integration exercise. No public rover specification, rover load case, measured vibration spectrum or planetary traction result was identified in this record.

title: GuaraniSat-2 mechanical properties and payload distribution
locator: 17 July 2025 drawing presentation, p. 2, Satellite properties, and p. 3, Isometric view (deployed configuration)

quantities.quantity: GuaraniSat-2 total mass listed in the drawing

conditions: AEP publishes separate bare-structure and overall stowed dimensions for the satellite. Its table specifies hardcoat-anodized 6061-T6 aluminum for the structure.
supports: Demonstrates why a payload drawing records the overall envelope and explicit stowed/deployed configuration as well as mass.
limits: A CubeSat drawing is an integration example. It supplies no public rover chassis dimensions, structural load rating or flight qualification for its use on a rover.

title: Paraguay’s COPUOS report on its deployed GuaraniSat-1 and planned sensor telemetry
locator: Republic of Paraguay statement, 2021 legal subcommittee, agenda item 3, pp. 3–5
conditions: Paraguay reported the March 2021 orbital deployment of GuaraniSat-1 and described plans for communicating field detector data through the satellite.
supports: An example of specifying the sensor, ground terminal and spacecraft as separate endpoints when designing telemetry.
limits: The statement records orbital deployment. It gives no measured link throughput, detector yield, or rover communications specification.
